answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to costly, verifiable work instead of free identities. Picture each agent as an island: it earns trust only by tending a shared garden of attestations, where each honest transaction plants a record peers can check and one lie poisons the plot. A newcomer faces a gale of entry costs: staking real collateral and finishing slow, peer-reviewed tasks before trading at scale. A thousand fake islands then cost a thousand stakes, while one honest agent pays once, so the attacker's bill grows linearly while the defense grows with each record.
